detailed_rationale:
Sanofi Consumer Healthcare India (SCHIL) is the OTC/consumer-health business demerged from Sanofi India in 2023, built around well-known branded categories: Combiflam (pain management), Allegra (allergy, 25+ years in the Indian market), Avil (allergy), and DePURA (Vitamin D). Because the entity has only traded independently since the demerger, several of our standard 3-year metrics (revenue CAGR, quality/value scores) are not computable yet -- this is a data-coverage limitation of a young listing, not a red flag on the business itself. On the numbers that are available: H1 FY26 revenue was Rs.4,649 million, Q2 FY26 revenue Rs.2,357 million with net profit Rs.919 million, and 1-year revenue growth of 38.3% -- though a meaningful part of that growth rate should be read with caution as a demerger-era base-effect (the comparison period likely still reflects transition-year noise), not a clean run-rate.

Balance sheet is clean: interest coverage of ~154.5x implies negligible net debt, and promoter (Sanofi global) holds 71.3%, a standard, low-governance-risk MNC-subsidiary ownership structure. The business benefits from strong brand equity in categories (pain relief, antihistamines) with real pricing power and repeat-purchase dynamics, and OTC/self-medication demand in India has a structural growth tailwind (urbanization, rising per-capita health spend, greater retail/e-pharmacy reach).

Reverse-DCF: at a P/E of ~40.7x, the market is paying up for brand-moat durability and margin quality rather than for the (likely non-recurring) 38% growth print. That valuation is full but defensible for a business with this kind of brand equity and balance-sheet strength, provided growth settles into a more sustainable low-double-digit range rather than continuing at the demerger-era pace.
recommendation_rationale: The quant Hold is reasonable: this is a fundamentally sound, brand-led consumer-health business with a clean balance sheet, but the valuation (~41x) already reflects that quality, and the very high trailing growth rate is partly a demerger-transition artifact rather than a clean structural run-rate. Nothing here supports an escalation toward Sell -- there is no balance-sheet or governance concern -- but nor is there a case that this is mispriced enough to be more attractive than Hold.
summary: Sanofi Consumer Healthcare India owns well-known OTC brands including Combiflam and Allegra, demerged from Sanofi India in 2023. The business has a clean, debt-free balance sheet and strong brand equity in categories with real repeat-purchase economics, but the reported 38% revenue growth partly reflects demerger-year comparison effects rather than a sustainable run-rate, and the stock's ~41x earnings multiple already prices in the brand quality. We rate this a Hold.
positive_para: Strong, long-standing consumer brands (Allegra has 25+ years of market presence) with real pricing power, a near debt-free balance sheet (interest coverage ~154x), and a majority MNC parent (Sanofi, 71.3% holding) that brings governance and R&D-pipeline comfort. OTC/self-medication demand in India carries a genuine structural growth tailwind.
negative_para: The headline 1-year revenue growth of 38.3% needs to be discounted for demerger-era base effects given the entity only began standalone reporting in 2023 -- this is very unlikely to be the sustainable run-rate. Several standard 3-year quality/value metrics are not yet computable given the short standalone history, which limits how confidently we can benchmark this name against peers, and the ~41x multiple leaves little room for a growth disappointment once the base normalizes.
reverse_dcf_judgment: At ~41x earnings, the market is pricing durable brand-moat economics and margin quality, not the reported 38% growth rate (which we read as partly a demerger-comparison artifact). Fair for the brand quality and balance-sheet strength; would become rich if growth settles meaningfully below low-double-digits once the base normalizes.
